argument:
The bear correctly treats3.60% adjusted FCF yield as more restrained than6.30x forecast earnings. Importantly, the cash normalisation already deducts $2.476bn new-business-model prepayments and $275m Flash Ventures net investment, leaving $8.743bn annual adjusted FCF. The positive case therefore survives a sizeable adjustment to reported cash rather than capitalising headline profit alone.

Debt also fell from $1.849bn to zero, giving observed financing improvement as well as $4.762bn cash. These facts cannot stabilise NAND prices, but provide capacity to absorb a softer cycle. Customer deposits and commitments still constrain availability, and79.20% adjusted quarterly operating margin should not be treated as permanent. A bullish purchase rests on cash-normalised resilience and customer growth through variable pricing, without predicting imminent reversal or assuming peak earnings recur.
key_points: Adjusted cash already removes substantial prepayment/investment contributions.
Debt repayment is observed rather than a forecast.
Through-cycle cash value remains more relevant than peak-sensitive P/E.
rebuttal_to_previous: I agree the cycle yield is modest. Yet adjusted FCF remains$8.743bn after major deductions and stated debt has actually fallen to zero. That strengthens resilience and financing freedom without claiming permanent pricing or unrestricted deposits; the buy argument uses adjusted cash rather than peak forward cheapness.
